title: Does Automated Flagging improve discernment or just shift response bias?
hypothesis: Accurate labels raise both AI-post and real-post accuracy relative to control; uninformative labels shift the share of 'AI' responses without improving overall accuracy.
primary_outcome: Discernment: hit rate on AI posts minus false-alarm rate on real posts (d-prime secondary).
comparison: Accurate labels vs uninformative labels vs no label.
rationale: Automated Flagging raised total accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [1.4, 7.3]), but total accuracy cannot separate real discernment from a bias toward answering 'AI'. Randomising label validity (accurate vs uninformative) lets a gain from accurate labels beyond the uninformative arm indicate discernment, while the share of 'AI' responses indicates bias.
contribution: Separates sensitivity from response bias in the automated-flagging effect by manipulating label informativeness.
unresolved: Actual image and video files and label overlays must be supplied by the research team
IRB number and compensation to be set by the research team

title: Does Automated Flagging hold when detector labels are imperfect?
hypothesis: Labels at 90% reliability raise accuracy relative to no labels; labels at 60% reliability do not raise accuracy and lower it on posts where the label is wrong.
comparison: High-reliability labels vs no labels vs low-reliability labels; secondary: accuracy on label-incorrect posts, and confidence in AI detection.
rationale: Automated Flagging raised total accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [1.4, 7.3]) while the pooled effect across 11 arms was only +1.0 point (95% CI [-0.3, 2.4]). Real detectors err, so we test whether the gain survives lower label reliability, a context the source did not cover, and whether people over-rely on wrong labels.
contribution: Maps the range of label reliability within which automated AI-detection labels help rather than mislead.
unresolved: Actual image files and per-image label assignments must be supplied by the research team
Compensation and IRB number to be supplied by the research team

title: Does a brief AI Literacy Guide or a mindfulness exercise change AI-media accuracy in an adequately powered replication?
hypothesis: The Guide raises total accuracy and mindfulness lowers it relative to control, in both weighted and unweighted estimates.
primary_outcome: Share of posts judged correctly (AI or authentic).
comparison: Guide vs control and Mindfulness vs control on total accuracy, reported unweighted and with IPW.
rationale: In the source study the AI Literacy Guide (+4.7 points, CI barely above zero) and Mindfulness (-3.9 points) effects depended on IPW weighting, and arms had only 78 to 181 respondents. This design replicates both against a control with equal, larger arms and pre-specifies weighted and unweighted estimates.
contribution: Gives a well-powered, pre-specified replication of the two weight-dependent accuracy effects with weighted and unweighted estimates reported side by side.
unresolved: Actual image files and the full set of 12 stimuli must be supplied by the research team
IRB approval number and compensation must be supplied by the research team
